PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

31 -> 0. The write stopped being silent on 2026-08-28: mixin.order.line.amount._check_write_derived_quantity refuses product_uom_qty from create and from write alike (fed310f743c), so every site this gate was counting had been a red test since August rather than drift to walk down. Appendix A and this gate's own summary both still described the silent behaviour and are corrected in 054fd26e089.

Swept in one commit: 33 writes across 21 test files, every one a fixture building an order line, none of them a place where the reference unit was the point.

33 against a floor of 31 because two sites were shapes the scan could not see, and both were found by a suite failing rather than by the gate. `order.line_ids = [Command.create({...})]` -- the assignment branch read only `<order line>.product_uom_qty = value`, so a command list assigned straight to the one2many was invisible although it reaches exactly the rows a write of that list reaches; closed in the same commit and pinned by test_assigning_a_command_list_to_the_o2m_is_a_write beside its negative twin on picking.move_ids, where the field is real. And a payload the call site named: test_event_full's test_event_mail built order_line_vals into a variable and passed it to write on the next line, which a scan of dict literals cannot see; still open, because resolving a name to its dict is local dataflow rather than a shape test.

Zero is what makes that remaining gap survivable: with nothing banked, the next literal site fails the gate the day it lands, and only the named-dict form can still arrive quietly. Kept as a file rather than deleted because this note is the record of how it got here (section 9.2: driven to zero -> keep the file).

Measured 0 on a clean detached worktree of 054fd26e089.
